# A simpler way in {sparkle}
RecordLah! opens on three choices: record what you are hearing now,
schedule a meeting, or watch what it recorded. Scheduling asks three
things -- the link, when it starts, whether it repeats. Everything else
is one button away, and Settings decides which screen you open on.

# Control it from your phone {iphone}
Turn on Settings > Phone, scan the code, approve it on the Mac. Then you
can schedule a recording and see what is happening without going back to
the Mac. Off, there is nothing listening. Part of the licence, and not in
the free trial -- and if a licence ever lapses, your phones stay
connected: adding one back switches the remote on again with nothing to
scan.

---

Everything else in this release:

- A recording in progress now looks like one: a red mark, a ticking
  clock, and one Stop button. Its own page shows what it is doing,
  whether your voice is in it, and the last lines it heard.
- The free trial says how many recordings are left -- and if the next one
  will not record, it says so before you press.
- Your recordings have a simple page: the list, the transcript, the notes.
- Search the transcript beside a recording. Press a match and the video
  jumps to that moment.
- The welcome screen lets you pick the simple or the advanced view, with a
  picture of each.
- Paste a link wrapped by your email (Safelinks, urldefense) and it is
  unwrapped for you. A Teams or Meet link is named, not just refused.
- A refusal keeps what you typed: the link stays in the box, the reason
  sits under it.
- Clearer words on the advanced screens -- "Recordings" not "Done",
  "Scheduled" not "Enabled", and a meeting that is not saved says so.
- Shift-Command-N schedules a recording. Command-N still opens the full
  editor.
